findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signs are not posted in the public restrooms. Per Assistant Manager, there are two sets of employee restrooms available for use, which is preferred. However, staff may also use the public restrooms. Handwashing signs are needed in all restrooms used by staff. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 General accumulation of mold, dirt, and old food debris were observed in fresh produce bins. Cleaning frequency was discussed. Produce department staff were advised as to the conditions and started cleaning during inspection. Additional cleaning is needed in the cold case by the entrance (see #49). Management and staff need time to allow for proper cleaning and sanitization throughout the produce cases in question, so additional time is being given to accomplish this task.
Ensure liners are replaced, and surfaces under liners are cleaned and sanitized. Ensure removable inserts that divide products are cleaned and sanitized at the 3 part sink. These cleaning and sanitization practices need to happen at a frequency that does not allow for accumulation of mold, dirt, and old food debris as was observed today. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Solution in sani-bucket used to start wiping down the back wall in the produce case was at 0ppm quat. Fresh solution was provided at 200ppm. Ensure use of quat test strips to verify sanitizer is at proper concentration when dispensed for use. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Ensure product is maintained at 150-400ppm as required per product label directions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
1) produce case where commercially processed packages of leafy greens are located by the entrance (mold on back wall);
2) shelving and inserts on shelves in the milk cooler (mold/general buildup); and
3) surfaces around door seals at milk cooler (splash/general debris). 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 1) Two tiles were missing from the floor in the first stall of the women’s employee restroom by upstairs break area. Small cracks were present in the subfloor. Seal the subfloor and/or replace the tiles. 
2) Caulking was observed worn at the juncture between the urinal and the wall in the men’s employee restroom upstairs by offices. Re-seal the area.
3) Caulking was observed worn at the juncture between the handwashing sink and the wall in the women’s employee restroom upstairs by offices. Re-seal the area.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 1) Mopsink was observed with heavy buildup of black debris along outer edges, assumed to be dirt and possibly some mold. Mopsink needs to be detail cleaned.
2) Floor was soiled with dried food splash and general debris along the doors at the reach-in section of the milk cooler.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-305.11: Observed a backpack inside the milk walk in cooler sitting on top of a milk container. Ensure that employee items are stored in a designated area. 
(A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed stained/mildewed ceiling tiles throughout the retail portion of the store. Tiles above the frozen foods and near the dairy products were especially bad. Discussed with PIC who stated that they replace the worst tiles as needed. Replace tiles and repair pipes as needed. Inspector will reassess at next routine inspection.
6-501.11

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a crock pot of beef and green peppers that had been cooled. Facility is a medium risk facility and therefore any cooked items that are not consumed that day must be discarded. Beef was discarded. 
750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: CORRECTED> Observed a breaded stuffing mixture dated 10/26 and a jalepeno meat stuffing mixture with no date in the small meat room walk in. Label all potentially hazardous foods with the date of preparation and hold no longer than 7 days from that date. Breaded stuffing was discarded and jalepeno mix was dated with Tuesday's date as it was made Tuesday.
findings.citation_text: 750.140 Potentially hazardous foods shall be labeled with the date of preparation and held no longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed turkey tenderloins thawing at ambient air temperature in the meat department. Use a proper thawing method which includes thawing in a cooler, thawing under cool, running water, thawing as part of the cooking process. Tenderloins were moved to the walk in cooler.
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be in need of repair: 1) there are numerous carts and metal shelves throughout the facility that are rusty (in the meat cutting room, in the walk in coolers, etc) 2) the door to the large walk in freezer that holds ice cream and retail items is in disrepair with the seal and metal sheeting separating from the door which does not allow the door to close completely creating a build up of ice in this area. Repair carts, shelves and door.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the scoops and the scoop holders in the self serve granola area to be soiled. Wash, rinse and sanitize scoops and holders.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the inside of the meat room display cases with old/dry meat crumbs 2) the electrical plug area in the walk in cooler near the meat grinder 3) cords from mechanical equipment in the meat cutting room are soiled with debris build up 4)the heat wrapper in the meat cutting room is soiled with debris under the warm plate 5) the containers holding the seasonings in the meat cutting room are heavily soiled with seasoning accumulation 6) the auto wrapper machine in the meat cutting room is heavily soiled with food debris build up underneath the stainless plates 7) the milk reach in/display coolers have plastic wrap underneath the shelves that is soiled. Clean all non-food contact areas.750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment:
Observed the meat department to be re-using 5 gallon icing buckets from the bakery to marinate meats. The re-use of single serve buckets is prohibited. Use re-usable food grade containers.
750-600 Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floors to be soiled in the following areas: 1) there is water in front of the fish display case 2) there is a build up of dirt accumulation in front of the fish display case 3) there is water on the floor in the large walk in cooler 4) the floor drains in the meat cutting room especially under the hand sink and near the auto wrapper are soiled with dirt and debris accumulation 5) the floors in the milk walk in are soiled with debris and freshly spilled milk 6) the floors in the daily walk in have plastic underneath the shelves that is soiled 7)there is water on the floor in the produce walk in cooler. Maintain the floors to be clean.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Observed the walls and/or ceilings to be soiled or in disrepair in the following areas: 1) behind the grinder 2) at the wall/floor junction behind the grinder 2) the wall behind the styrofoam trays in the meat cutting room is soiled 3) there are several small holes in the wall along the three compartment sink wall in the meat cutting room 4) there is a stainless steel wall panel piece that is separating from the wall in the meat cutting room and creating gaps in the wall 5) coving is missing in this same area where the panel is separating 6) a couple ceiling tiles in the dairy walk in cooler are broken. Clean and/or repair walls and ceilings. 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
REPEAT> Observed broken light shields in the dairy walk in cooler. Replace light shield.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a spray bottle in the small meat department walk in cooler that did not have a label and a spray bottle in the chemical storage room near the restrooms to not be labeled. Label all chemical spray bottle with the contents name. Spray bottles were labeled. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.
